summary:
Cosmic Relics: The Mechanical Footprints of Human Exploration is a narrative-driven digital presentation designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the remarkable engineering history of hardware left behind by NASA across the solar system.

What we developed: A visual, story-based concept deck that serves as an interactive "space archaeology" guide, chronicling iconic artifacts from the Apollo lunar module descent stages and Martian robotic landers to deep-space probes like Voyager.

How it addresses the challenge: Instead of technical code, it translates complex mechanical and aerospace engineering accomplishments into engaging, accessible storytelling tailored specifically for young learners, satisfying the core objective of highlighting discarded equipment and the science it enabled.

Why it is important: It transforms silent relics of metal and circuits into inspiring educational monuments, preserving the legacy of past missions and sparking curiosity for the next generation of engineers and explorers.
details:
• What it does and how it works:
    Cosmic Relics: The Mechanical Footprints of Human Exploration functions as a digital space archaeology guide. It systematically documents, categorizes, and narrates the history of physical hardware and scientific equipment left behind by NASA across the solar system—including lunar module descent stages on the Moon, stationary rovers and heat shields on Mars, and deep-space probes like Voyager. It operates through structured, story-driven visual presentations that translate complex engineering accomplishments into accessible narratives.
    • Educational Benefit: It bridges the gap between aerospace engineering history and public engagement, specifically targeting school-age space enthusiasts.
    • Intended Impact: To inspire the next generation of engineers, scientists, and explorers by reframing abandoned technology not as waste, but as permanent monuments of human ingenuity and footprints of our technological evolution.
    • Creativity: It reframes traditional space exploration projects—which usually focus entirely on active missions—into a unique "space archaeology" perspective, looking at the lasting physical heritage left on planetary bodies.
    • Factors Considered: Simplicity of design, clear structural hierarchy, mechanical durability of materials in extreme space environments, and engaging storytelling appropriate for younger audiences.
